- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (forecast > true by >10%) — apply downward correction of 5–15% if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- Lagged mean reversion: if 10-day moving average of true prices is below forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment > 0.4 and forecast > true by >5%, cap forecast at 10% below peak or 15% below 5-day high.
- Discount sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment > 0.3 and forecast > true by >10%, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs: if last 3 days of forecast are > 10% above true, reduce by 5–10% for next 5 days regardless of sentiment.
- Use sentiment as a volatility filter: if sentiment < 0.1, reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30-day horizon to avoid overconfidence in low sentiment.
- Apply downward bias correction if true price drops > 5% from 10-day average — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days.
